name: rare-trigger-severe

finding.title: Two saves at once write the same temporary file and can corrupt the settings file
finding.description: Every `save` writes to the same `<path>.tmp`. When the Save button runs while the autosave thread is still writing, `open(tmp, "w")` truncates the other thread's half-written file, and one of the two `os.replace` calls moves a mix of both writes over the settings file. The next `load` fails on the broken JSON and the user's settings are gone. Both callers are named in the class docstring.

checks: store/settings.py:16 every call uses the same temporary path
store/settings.py:17 opens it with `w`, which truncates it
store/settings.py:19 replaces the settings file with it

finding.suggestedFix: Write to a unique temporary file per call, such as one from `tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(dir=..., delete=False)`, or hold a lock across the write and the replace.

+import json
+import os
+
+
+class SettingsStore:
+    """Keeps a user's settings in one JSON file.
+
+    The editor's autosave thread calls `save` every 30 seconds, and the
+    Save button calls it from the UI thread.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, path: str):
+        self._path = path
+
+    def save(self, settings: dict) -> None:
+        tmp = self._path + ".tmp"
+        with open(tmp, "w") as f:
+            json.dump(settings, f)
+        os.replace(tmp, self._path)
+
+    def load(self) -> dict:
+        with open(self._path) as f:
+            return json.load(f)
